An independently selected complex everyday scene for testing visible domestic place, in-progress tidying action, background, and prop relations. The coordinator specified the test family as returning one object to its place in a neat but actively used home; this is an evaluation condition, not requester text. The supplied portrait guides visible adult appearance only.

An editorial lifestyle photograph of one unmistakably adult woman in a compact apartment living room that looks neat yet actively used. Her visible appearance takes loose guidance from the supplied portrait: long dark softly waved hair parted near the center and a calm face. She is midway through returning a closed blue paperback to the narrow gap between upright books on an oak shelf. Her left palm supports the lower edge of the book while her right fingertips steady its upper edge; the book is halfway inserted, its fore-edge entering the gap and its spine still projecting from the row. She stands on both feet close to the shelf with her elbows naturally bent, and the open shelf faces the camera. A glass of water sits on a side table beside a pale sofa with slightly compressed cushions; a pleated lamp stands on a sideboard, and a small plant brightens the window sill. Clear overcast daylight reveals the lived-in order, her touching hands, the half-returned book, and its exact target gap in one medium-wide frame.
